## Purpose

This SOP describes standard polymerase chain reaction (PCR) amplification
of target DNA fragments and visualization of PCR products by agarose gel
electrophoresis. PCR is used in the EA Program for confirming DNA
extraction success, screening for target genes before ddPCR or
sequencing, and verifying amplicon size and specificity prior to library
preparation [@mullis1990; @lorenz2012]. Gel electrophoresis separates DNA
fragments by size, providing a visual confirmation that amplification
produced the expected product.


## Scope

- **Applies to:** Standard endpoint PCR amplification of environmental
  DNA extracts (soil, water, tissue) and visualization of products on
  agarose gels; applicable to gene-specific screening, amplicon
  verification, and colony PCR
- **Does not apply to:** Quantitative PCR (qPCR) or digital PCR (ddPCR;
  see [SOP-L701](SOP-L701-ddpcr-nitrogen-cycle-primers.qmd) and
  [SOP-L702](SOP-L702-ddpcr-data-analysis.qmd)); RT-PCR for RNA targets;
  polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis (PAGE)
- **Location:** Molecular biology bench, SGM 133


## Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                              |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------|
| Lab PI            | Approve primer selections and cycling protocols |
| Trained Personnel | Set up PCR reactions and run gels per this SOP |
| New Students      | Complete training before independent use    |


## Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Chemical:** Ethidium bromide (EtBr) and SYBR Safe are nucleic acid
  stains. EtBr is a suspected mutagen; handle with gloves at all times
  and dispose of gels and buffers as hazardous waste. SYBR Safe is a
  safer alternative but should still be handled with gloves.
- **Electrical:** Gel electrophoresis uses high voltage (80--120 V). Do
  not touch the buffer or gel while the power supply is on. Always
  disconnect the leads before opening the gel box.
- **UV radiation:** Transilluminators emit UV light that can cause skin
  burns and eye damage. Use a UV shield, wear UV-blocking safety glasses,
  and minimize exposure time. Blue-light transilluminators are preferred
  when used with SYBR Safe.
- **Biological:** Environmental DNA extracts may originate from samples
  containing pathogens. Handle with standard precautions.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Safety glasses (UV-blocking if using a UV transilluminator)
- [ ] Lab coat
- [ ] Nitrile gloves (change frequently; required at all times when
      handling gels, stains, or PCR products)

### Emergency Procedures

For EtBr contact with skin, wash immediately with soap and water. For
UV exposure, flush eyes with water and seek medical attention. Refer to
[SOP-L003 Hazardous Materials Handling](SOP-L003-hazardous-materials-handling.qmd).


## Equipment and Materials

### Equipment

| Item                              | Location         | Notes                          |
|:----------------------------------|:-----------------|:-------------------------------|
| Thermal cycler (Bio-Rad C1000 Touch or equivalent) | Mol bio bench | Verify block type matches tube format |
| Gel electrophoresis system (tank, comb, casting tray) | Mol bio bench | Mini-gel (7 x 10 cm) or midi-gel |
| Power supply                      | Mol bio bench    | Capable of 10--300 V           |
| Gel imaging system (transilluminator + camera) | Mol bio bench | UV or blue-light; with gel documentation software |
| Micropipettes (2, 10, 100, 1000 uL) | Mol bio bench | Calibrated annually            |
| Microwave                         | Lab              | For melting agarose            |
| Microcentrifuge                   | Mol bio bench    | For brief spin-downs           |

### Reagents and Consumables

| Item                                  | Notes                              |
|:--------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------|
| Taq DNA polymerase or high-fidelity polymerase | e.g., GoTaq (Promega), Q5 (NEB), or OneTaq (NEB) |
| 5x or 10x PCR buffer (with MgCl~2~)  | Supplied with polymerase           |
| dNTP mix (10 mM each)                | Store at --20 C                    |
| Forward and reverse primers (10 uM working stocks) | Store at --20 C |
| Nuclease-free water                   | For master mix and negative controls |
| PCR tubes or plates (0.2 mL, thin-wall) | Matched to thermal cycler block  |
| Agarose (molecular biology grade)     | For gel preparation                |
| 1x TAE or TBE buffer                  | Running buffer; prepare from 50x stock |
| DNA stain (SYBR Safe or ethidium bromide) | SYBR Safe preferred              |
| DNA ladder (100 bp and/or 1 kb)       | e.g., NEB 100 bp or 1 kb Plus    |
| 6x gel loading dye                    | Often included with ladder or polymerase |
| Filter pipette tips (10, 100, 1000 uL) | Barrier tips mandatory to prevent cross-contamination |


## Procedure

### PCR Workspace Preparation

::: {.callout-important}
### Contamination Prevention

PCR is extremely sensitive to contamination. Follow these rules:

- Set up reactions in a designated pre-PCR area, physically separated
  from post-PCR work (gel loading, product analysis).
- Never bring PCR products, gels, or gel imaging equipment into the
  pre-PCR area.
- Use dedicated pipettes for pre-PCR work. Use filter tips exclusively.
- Wipe bench surfaces with 10% bleach followed by 70% ethanol before
  setting up reactions.
- Change gloves frequently, especially after touching any surface
  outside the pre-PCR area.
:::

### Master Mix Preparation

Prepare all components on ice. Calculate volumes for the number of
reactions plus 10% overage to account for pipetting losses.

**Standard 25 uL reaction (GoTaq example):**

| Component                  | Volume per reaction | Final concentration |
|:---------------------------|:--------------------|:--------------------|
| 5x GoTaq Reaction Buffer   | 5.0 uL              | 1x                  |
| dNTP mix (10 mM each)      | 0.5 uL              | 200 uM each         |
| Forward primer (10 uM)     | 1.25 uL             | 500 nM              |
| Reverse primer (10 uM)     | 1.25 uL             | 500 nM              |
| GoTaq DNA Polymerase (5 U/uL) | 0.125 uL         | 0.625 U             |
| Nuclease-free water        | 14.875 uL           | --                  |
| **Subtotal (master mix)**  | **23.0 uL**         |                     |
| Template DNA               | 2.0 uL              | Variable (1--10 ng) |
| **Total**                  | **25.0 uL**         |                     |

1. Thaw buffer, dNTPs, and primers on ice. Vortex briefly and spin down.
2. Prepare the master mix in a sterile 1.5 mL tube, adding polymerase
   last. Mix by pipetting; do not vortex.
3. Aliquot 23 uL of master mix into each labeled PCR tube.
4. Add 2 uL of template DNA to each tube. Include controls:
   - **Positive control:** DNA known to amplify with these primers
   - **Negative control (NTC):** 2 uL of nuclease-free water
   - **Extraction blank:** DNA extract from
     [SOP-L700](SOP-L700-dna-extraction.qmd) extraction blank
5. Cap tubes, vortex briefly, and spin down.

### Thermal Cycling

Program the thermal cycler with the following general protocol. Adjust
the annealing temperature for your specific primer set.

| Step                   | Temperature | Time     | Cycles |
|:-----------------------|:------------|:---------|:-------|
| Initial denaturation   | 95 C        | 2 min    | 1      |
| Denaturation           | 95 C        | 30 s     | 30--35 |
| Annealing              | *T~a~* C    | 30 s     | 30--35 |
| Extension              | 72 C        | 1 min/kb | 30--35 |
| Final extension        | 72 C        | 5 min    | 1      |
| Hold                   | 4 C         | Hold     | --     |

where *T~a~* is the annealing temperature, typically 3--5 C below the
lower primer T~m~. For primers with T~m~ of 55--60 C, start at 55 C.
Optimize by running a gradient if needed [@lorenz2012].

Record the cycling parameters, primer names, and annealing temperature
in the lab notebook.

### Agarose Gel Preparation

1. Weigh agarose for a 1--2% gel (w/v), depending on the expected
   amplicon size:

| Agarose % | Effective separation range |
|:----------|:--------------------------|
| 0.8%      | 500--10,000 bp            |
| 1.0%      | 250--7,000 bp             |
| 1.5%      | 100--3,000 bp             |
| 2.0%      | 50--1,500 bp              |

2. Add agarose to 1x TAE (or TBE) buffer in an Erlenmeyer flask.
3. Microwave in 30-second intervals, swirling between intervals, until
   the agarose is fully dissolved and the solution is clear.
4. Cool to approximately 55 C (comfortable to hold).
5. If using SYBR Safe, add 5 uL per 50 mL of gel. Swirl gently.
6. Pour into the casting tray with the comb in place. Allow to solidify
   (approximately 20--30 minutes at room temperature).

### Loading and Running the Gel

1. Remove the comb carefully. Place the gel in the electrophoresis tank
   and fill with 1x TAE (or TBE) buffer until the gel is submerged by
   2--3 mm.
2. Load 5 uL of DNA ladder into the first well.
3. Add loading dye to each PCR product (if not already included in the
   PCR buffer). Load 5--10 uL per well.
4. Record the loading order in the lab notebook.
5. Connect the leads: DNA migrates toward the positive (red) electrode.
   Confirm the orientation.
6. Run at 80--120 V for 30--45 minutes, or until the leading dye front
   has migrated approximately two-thirds of the gel length.
7. Turn off the power supply and disconnect the leads before removing
   the gel.

### Gel Imaging

1. Place the gel on the transilluminator (blue light for SYBR Safe;
   UV for EtBr).
2. Capture an image using the gel documentation system.
3. Save the image with the naming convention:
   `YYYY-MM-DD_primers_project_gel.tif`
4. Evaluate the image:
   - Positive control: visible band at the expected size
   - NTC and extraction blank: no visible band
   - Samples: band at the expected size indicates successful
     amplification
5. Upload the image to the project GitHub repository under
   `results/gels/`.


## Troubleshooting

| Symptom                    | Probable Cause                     | Corrective Action                     |
|:---------------------------|:-----------------------------------|:--------------------------------------|
| No bands in any lane       | Failed reaction; wrong cycling parameters | Check primer and dNTP stocks; verify cycling program |
| Bands in NTC               | Contamination                      | Discard reagents; clean workspace with bleach; use fresh aliquots |
| Multiple bands             | Non-specific amplification         | Increase annealing temperature; reduce primer concentration; redesign primers |
| Smear instead of band      | DNA degradation or overloaded gel   | Reduce template amount; check DNA quality on NanoDrop |
| Bands too faint             | Insufficient template or cycles    | Increase template to 5--10 ng; increase to 35 cycles |
| Bands in samples but not positive control | Positive control degraded | Prepare fresh positive control DNA |


## Quality Control

- Every PCR run must include: positive control, NTC, and extraction blank
- No bands should appear in the NTC or extraction blank. Any
  amplification in controls invalidates the run [@salter2014].
- Band size must match the expected amplicon size (compare to the DNA
  ladder)
- For quantitative downstream applications (library prep, sequencing),
  confirm band intensity is roughly uniform across samples


## Waste Disposal

| Waste Type                    | Container                 | Disposal Method                     |
|:------------------------------|:--------------------------|:------------------------------------|
| EtBr-stained gels and buffer | Designated EtBr waste container | EH&S hazardous waste pickup    |
| SYBR Safe-stained gels       | Standard trash (check local EH&S policy) | Non-hazardous per manufacturer |
| Used PCR tubes and tips       | Standard trash            | Non-hazardous after thermal cycling |
| Unused EtBr stock solution    | Chemical waste            | EH&S hazardous waste pickup         |

## Training Record

Before performing PCR and gel electrophoresis independently, personnel
must:

1. Read this SOP and [SOP-L700](SOP-L700-dna-extraction.qmd) in full
2. Demonstrate master mix preparation with correct volumes and controls
3. Run a supervised PCR and gel, producing a clean positive control
   band with no NTC contamination
4. Demonstrate safe handling of DNA stains and proper gel disposal
5. Be signed off by the PI or lab manager
